courseDetails.title: Rischi dell'IA generativa e cybersecurity: sicurezza LLM
courseDetails.shortDescription: Attaccate e difendete gli LLM in pratica: prompt injection, jailbreak, guardrail, red teaming e conformità
courseDetails.longDescription:
In questo corso vengono utilizzati strumenti di intelligenza artificiale.

Che cosa aspettarsi: circa 5 ore di video. Prevedete 1 ora per installare gli strumenti del laboratorio (Ollama e un modello locale), poi circa 9–12 ore per svolgere i 14 laboratori e i relativi esercizi. Tutti i laboratori funzionano in un unico file sul vostro computer, con un modello Llama locale e gratuito tramite Ollama: non servono chiavi API né account a pagamento. L'interfaccia del laboratorio, i prompt di attacco digitati e le risposte del modello restano in inglese.

L'IA generativa è arrivata in produzione più velocemente delle pratiche di sicurezza in grado di proteggerla. Prompt injection, jailbreak, avvelenamento dei dati, allucinazioni sfruttate: gli attacchi contro i modelli linguistici di grandi dimensioni non somigliano a quelli che i team di sicurezza conoscono. In questo corso impariamo a comprenderli, a eseguirli in un ambiente sicuro e poi a costruire le difese che li fermano.

Tutto il corso segue un'azienda fittizia, NovaStar AI, e i suoi tre prodotti: NovaAssist, un chatbot di assistenza clienti, NovaCode, un assistente di programmazione, e NovaComply, uno strumento di documentazione normativa. Con il CISO Alex Rivera e il suo team analizziamo ogni incidente, riproduciamo l'attacco in laboratorio e poi introduciamo il controllo che l'avrebbe impedito.

In nove sezioni:

  • Mappiamo la superficie di attacco di un'applicazione LLM con l'OWASP Top 10 per le applicazioni LLM e MITRE ATLAS
  • Eseguiamo prompt injection dirette e indirette e jailbreak contro un modello locale
  • Trattiamo avvelenamento dei dati, bias, SSRF, esaurimento delle risorse e allucinazioni come minacce
  • Costruiamo una difesa in profondità: validazione degli input, guardrail, filtraggio degli output, isolamento e monitoraggio
  • Integriamo la sicurezza nel ciclo di sviluppo e conduciamo esercitazioni di red teaming
  • Affrontiamo il regolamento europeo sull'intelligenza artificiale (AI Act), il NIST AI RMF, la ISO/IEC 42001, gli audit e la proprietà intellettuale
  • Anticipiamo le minacce dell'IA agentica, dell'IA contro l'IA e del calcolo quantistico

Ogni sezione si chiude con un quiz e il corso termina con un'esercitazione completa di red teaming che mette insieme tutto ciò che avete imparato. Ne uscite con un metodo concreto per valutare, attaccare e mettere in sicurezza i sistemi di IA generativa della vostra organizzazione.

Did you open this page specifically to avoid the task you are supposed to be doing right now?

Take a breath. You are not lazy, you do not lack willpower, and nothing is broken in you. Your brain is doing exactly what it evolved to do.

For years we were told that beating procrastination meant buying another planner, installing ten more productivity apps, or simply trying harder. Modern psychology and neuroscience, led by researchers like Dr. Tim Pychyl (Carleton University) and Dr. Fuschia Sirois, proved something far more freeing: procrastination is not a time management problem, it is an emotion regulation problem.

You do not put things off because you cannot read a clock. You put them off because the task triggers an uncomfortable feeling (boredom, fear of failing, frustration, uncertainty) and the most impulsive part of your brain grabs the wheel to hand you instant relief.

Why this course is different from every other productivity course

Most courses hand you twenty theories, leave you feeling inspired for an afternoon, and change nothing by Monday. The ultimate irony: procrastinating on fixing your procrastination.

This course runs on one rule. Across the modules you will hit 7 guided exercises called DO IT NOW, built so you take real action on your phone, at your desk, and on your actual unfinished task while the lesson is still playing. You do not walk away with notes. You walk away with progress.

The tools you will master

  • The 2-Minute Rule (David Allen), to break inertia and start without waiting for motivation.

  • The Pomodoro Technique (Francesco Cirillo), to put walls and guaranteed breaks around any intimidating task.

  • The 20-Second Rule, to redesign your environment and shut down digital distractions.

  • Temptation bundling and friction reduction, so starting becomes the easiest thing you do all day.

GRASP is one of the most misunderstood and misused foundations of object oriented design. Many developers hear the names of the principles, but almost nobody knows how to apply them correctly, how they conflict, and how real design decisions are actually made. This course fixes that.

You will not just learn what each GRASP principle is.

You will learn how to think like a designer.


What makes this course different

This is not a definitions course.
This is a decision making course.

You will see:

  • Why GRASP is more fundamental than SOLID

  • Why many "best practices" directly violate GRASP

  • Why blindly following principles creates worse designs

  • How professional architects actually balance trade-offs

Every principle is explained through:

  • Clear mental models

  • Real domain driven examples

  • Explicit anti-patterns

  • Live refactoring and demos

  • Architectural context, not isolated classes


What you will learn

You will master responsibility assignment, which is the core skill behind all good object oriented systems.

Specifically, you will learn how to:

  • Identify the true Information Expert in a domain model instead of creating fake experts and data classes

  • Decide when Low Coupling is more important than perfect responsibility placement

  • Avoid God Controllers and correctly map system events to controllers

  • Design classes with High Cohesion and detect cohesion violations early

  • Replace conditionals with Polymorphism only when it actually improves the design

  • Use Pure Fabrication without turning your system into a service soup

  • Apply Indirection to reduce coupling without destroying clarity

  • Protect unstable parts of the system using Protected Variations and abstractions

Each topic includes:

  • Correct examples

  • Incorrect examples

  • Clear explanation of why one design fails and the other works


Beyond individual principles

GRASP principles do not work in isolation. This course explicitly teaches how they interact.

You will understand:

  • Why Information Expert often conflicts with Low Coupling

  • Why Polymorphism and Protected Variations reinforce each other

  • How Controller decisions impact cohesion and coupling across layers

  • How to choose the dominant principle when rules conflict

This is the part most courses completely ignore.


GRASP in real architecture

GRASP is not just about classes.

You will see how it applies across architectural layers:

  • Domain layer: responsibility, behavior, and modeling

  • Application layer: orchestration and control flow

  • Infrastructure layer: boundaries, indirection, and change isolation

  • Clear cases where GRASP should not be applied at all

You will stop misusing GRASP where it does not belong.


GRASP vs SOLID vs GoF

This course clearly explains:

  • What problems GRASP actually solves

  • Why SOLID came later and builds on GRASP ideas

  • How GoF patterns emerge naturally from GRASP decisions

  • How to map GRASP principles to SOLID and GoF without cargo culting

After this section, design principles will finally make sense as a system, not a checklist.


Who this course is for

This course is ideal if you:

  • Write object oriented code but feel your designs degrade over time

  • Know SOLID but struggle to apply it consistently

  • Want to move from "code that works" to code that lasts

  • Aim to think like a senior engineer or software architect

  • Are tired of vague advice and want clear design reasoning


Outcome

After completing this course, you will:

  • Design classes with confidence

  • Explain and defend your design decisions

  • Recognize bad designs immediately

  • Apply GRASP naturally, not mechanically

  • Write systems that are easier to change, test, and extend

This course does not teach rules.

It teaches judgment.
